title: Ven Diagram
note: Diagrams are redrawn (D29), not cut from the photos: each is a set of circles (Q39-40: rectangles, four lines each) in a clean layout that keeps every printed relation, which shapes are apart, which overlap and which sit inside which; sizes and positions are not the photo's. Ovals are drawn as circles. Where a question gives the classes and asks for the diagram, `options` describes each drawn answer in words for screen readers and `answerPanels` draws it. Where a diagram is given and the options are classes (Q9, 25, 44-48), the diagram is `figure` and `stem` describes it. A square or rectangle printed round the circles (Q4, 5, 20, 21, 22, 31, 41, 42, 43) is drawn as four lines round them; it is the whole page, not a class. Printed letters and numbers inside circles (Q2, 13, 14, 17, 49, 50) are kept as labels, each set in the part of its circle that no smaller circle covers. Q4: the third circle in options A and B meets the others at a single point in the photo; it is read as touching, not overlapping, and drawn just clear of them. Q12 B: the third circle meets the inner circle at a point, read the same way. Q34 prints its four diagrams in a row lettered A-D above options that read only "(A) A (B) B (C) C (D) D"; it is set as the other questions are, each option drawn and described. Q41 begins with the stray word "classes." as printed, and lists four classes under a direction about three elements. The chapter direction prints "Q. No. 1 to 38"; Q39-48 have a second printed direction, and Q49-50 each print their own instruction, kept as its direction. Q49-50 print their statements on separate lines, kept as line breaks. Typos kept as printed: "Ven" in the title and direction, "Shripm" (Q1), "coardiologist" (Q2), "Unit,Watt" without a space (Q5), the full stop after "Village people" (Q6), "intense linkage" (direction Q39-48).

directions.text: Select the venn diagram that best represents the relationship between the following classes. And select the set of classes whose relationship between them is best represented by the following ven diagram.

Each of the questions given below contains three elements. These elements may or may not have some intense linkage. Each group of elements may fit into one of the diagrams lettered (A), (B), (C) or (D). You have to indicate the diagram in which the group of elements fit correctly.
Ignoring commonly known facts, read the following statements and then choose the Venn diagram from the four alternatives which best represents the given statements.
